Chapaṭa(chappada)
or saddhammajotipAla of Chapaṭa in Pagan, Burma; settled in Ceylon an. became a Thera; contemporary of Parākramabāhu VI of Kotte; mentioned in Kalyani inscriptions.
See Uni. Cey. Rev. IX. i. p.. 69-75.
--C. Saṅkhepavaṇṇanā on Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha. NCC. I. p. 288a.
--C. Suttaniddesa on Kaccāyana's Pāli gr. composed a. the request of his pupil Dhammacāri. Colombo D.

.
--Visuddhimagga-gaṇṭhi. See Uni. Cey. Rev. IX. i. p. 75.
Other works of his mentioned in

, p.. 88-92 an. Bode, Pāli Lit. of Burma p.. 17-19:
--Nāmacāradīpanī. on ethics; introduced into Burma.
--Gandha (i)sāra. anthology. NCC. V. p. 309a.
--Māṭikatthadīpanī on Abhidhamma.
--Paṭṭhānagaṇānaya on Abhidhamma.
--Vinayasamuṭṭhānadīpanī. written a. the request of a.'s preceptor.
--Vinayagūṭhatthadīpanī. explanation of difficult passages of Vinayapiṭaka.

Chappaccayadīpanī
Pāli prosody. by Saddhammañāṇa Thera, a. inhabitant of Pagan. Fausboll 173 (7).
See Ind. Cult. XV. p. 198; Bode, Pāli Lit. of Burma p. 26. [Page108-b]

Chappaṇṇaya_Gāhāvo
or Gāthākośa in 164 verses; mostly in Mahārāṣṭrī besides some in Apabhram3śa. by Vidagdhas. Cat. of Palm-leaf mss. in the Śāntinātha Jaina Bhaṇḍāra a. Cambay,

, Baroda, 1961. See J. of Ori. Res. Inst., M. S. Uni. Baroda, XI. p.. 385-402.
Pt.. a. app. to Saptaśatīsāra. with Skt. Chāyā. Shivaji Uni. Skt. & Pkt. Ser. Vol.

Chappada
of Ceylon; Bud. Thera, pupil of Sāriputra.
--C. on Sīmālaṅkārasaṅgraha of Mahāsāmi Vācissara, the librarian of Parākramabāhu I.
See Uni. Cey. Rev. IX. i. p.. 69 ff.

Chappannahorāśāstra
jy. a.. Gov. Or. Libr. Madras 28.

Chappāhuḍa(ṣaṭprābhṛta)
by Kundakunda. See Ṣaṭprābhṛta; also NCC. IV. p. 194b.
